change: Chunk-index copy-on-write snapshots share frozen cells. Shared buckets clone on edit. One-cell buckets store a direct local index; larger buckets use local integer keys. Stored/implicit cell reads are frozen. Apply remains the mutation API; no save/wire/limit changes.

tests.scope: The full selected run passed 65 tests; the focused rerun passed all three snapshot tests including the subsequently added 4096-coordinate case. Final retained reports total 66 distinct cases.
tests.coverage: Nested forks, clear/replay, negative chunk boundaries, all 4096 local indices, immutable cells, single-to-multi bucket transitions and 1000 randomized edit/fork/clear steps against independent reference maps; fractional geometry, saves, offline/TLS structures, occupancy, streaming and MP3 regressions.

probe.layout: Each JVM builds 100,000 Stone cells at x=0..499, z=0..199, y=128. Compact spacing 1 uses 416 chunks; scattered spacing 16 uses 100,000 chunks and deliberately represents global-world edits outside one structure footprint. Fixture setup and GC are excluded from timed operations.

probe.tradeoff: Snapshot allocation falls in both layouts. Compact first-edit allocation rises from 208 to 10,528 bytes because it clones a 256-cell bucket. Source retained-heap samples: compact 17,547,208/11,566,872 bytes, scattered 17,562,304/17,595,672 bytes (parent/current). Scattered memory is approximately unchanged within GC-sensitive sample noise. First-edit latency increases and scattered timings are noisy. Subsequent edits use the owned bucket.
probe.limits: One GC-sensitive retained-source sample per fixture/JVM is not peak memory. Three warmups and 20 timed samples per operation are synthetic CPU diagnostics while software native rendering runs; not city/max or frame/tick/network qualification.
probe.parent_source_capture: Python subprocess.check_output captured the parent Git source into target/structure-snapshot-parent-src/dev/jayms/net/WorldVoxels.java before compilation.
